claim: In the authors' robotic-ultrasound system, four probe-mounted time-of-flight sensors provided an independent observation of nearby body-surface orientation that supported real-time probe self-normal-positioning without preoperative surface information, with improved flat-surface angular accuracy after sensor calibration but substantially region-dependent errors on complex mannequin topography. The study also measured ultrasound image CNR as an endpoint not used by the surface-normal estimator. This supports the feasibility of separating local geometry observation from an independent imaging outcome, but it does not establish observability of finite contact area or pressure, a minimally sufficient contact representation, impedance-selection value, or statistically demonstrated equivalence of robotic and manual image quality.
claim_locator: System design and calibration; surface-normal and force-control methods; flat-surface and mannequin experiments; volunteer lung-ultrasound CNR comparison; limitations and future work
epistemic_status: Author-reported prototype and experimental evidence with a reader-qualified statistical interpretation of the image endpoint; implications for P-SOFTSCAN-STATE-01 v1 are explicitly limited to hypothesis and evaluation design.
problem_and_setting: A robotic curvilinear ultrasound probe mounted on a Franka Panda must align to the local body-surface normal in real time without preoperative surface information. Four ring-mounted time-of-flight laser range sensors observe nearby surface outside the probe housing; a separate normal-force loop uses robot joint-torque-estimated force, while the operator teleoperates tangential translation and axial rotation. Evaluation covers calibrated sensor distance, flat and upper-torso-mannequin normal tracking, a breathing lung-ultrasound phantom, and volunteer image acquisition at eight targets.
method_or_mechanism: Opposite-pair distance differences from four moving-average-filtered VL53L0X sensors drive empirical PD angular-velocity commands for the two probe tilt axes, capped at 0.1 rad/s and updated at up to 30 Hz. Lookup-table calibration compensates distance error over 50-200 mm. A distinct two-stage normal-translation controller performs landing and then tracks desired normal force using a joint-torque-based force estimate. Surface-normal ground truth is obtained by motion capture. Pleural-line image quality is assessed afterward using CNR from a manually defined fixed 10-by-10-pixel ROI; image CNR is not an input to the surface-normal estimator.
content_summary: Calibration reduced reported mean distance error from 11.03 plus-or-minus 1.61 mm to 3.19 plus-or-minus 1.97 mm. On a flat surface, the minimum normal error with compensation was 4.17 plus-or-minus 2.24 degrees versus 12.51 plus-or-minus 2.69 degrees without compensation, with response time about 3.67 plus-or-minus 0.84 s. Mannequin performance was less accurate and strongly region dependent: overall error was 14.67 plus-or-minus 8.46 degrees, including 28.76 plus-or-minus 8.84 degrees anteriorly, 17.80 plus-or-minus 8.46 degrees anterior-laterally, and 8.52 plus-or-minus 3.85 degrees laterally. Under simulated breathing, force error was mostly within plus-or-minus 1 N, with mean 0.07 plus-or-minus 0.49 N. Robotic and freehand volunteer scans produced overlapping reported CNR summaries, and conventional t-tests returned p values of 0.21, 0.28, and 0.53. The authors interpreted these nonsignificant results as equivalent image quality, but the study did not report a predeclared equivalence or noninferiority margin and repeated images and targets may be clustered.
synthesis_role: Supports OBL-SPATIAL-OBSERVABILITY and CHAIN-SPATIAL-SUFFICIENCY only in the specific sense that independent nearby-surface geometry can be sensed online and used for orientation control. It also supports OBL-INDEPENDENT-ENDPOINT by pairing sensor-based alignment with an image-quality outcome not used by the estimator. It does not show that the finite probe-tissue contact patch, contact area, pressure distribution, or local deformation is observed, and therefore does not establish the minimal sufficient contact representation. The large topography-dependent error is evidence that sensing outside the probe footprint can leave important geometry unobserved.
development_link: For P-SOFTSCAN-STATE-01 v1, the paper motivates retaining a strict separation among nearby surface-normal geometry, finite contact-patch state, normal-force feedback, and the independent imaging endpoint. A SoftScan evaluation can use a leakage-resistant held-out image endpoint to test decision value, but must not treat a surface-normal sensor as an independent contact-area measurement. Representation ablations should test whether contact-patch variables add value beyond external geometry and force-only baselines under held-out material and geometry shifts, with a predeclared equivalence or noninferiority margin if equivalence is claimed.

evidence.finding: Four ring-mounted time-of-flight sensors observe nearby surface outside the probe and use opposite-pair distance differences to control two tilt axes; this is local surface-orientation sensing rather than contact-area or pressure sensing.
Lookup-table compensation reduced mean distance error from 11.03 plus-or-minus 1.61 mm to 3.19 plus-or-minus 1.97 mm, with reported p equal to 9.72e-8.
Minimum normal error was 4.17 plus-or-minus 2.24 degrees with compensation versus 12.51 plus-or-minus 2.69 degrees without compensation, and response time was approximately 3.67 plus-or-minus 0.84 s.
Overall normal error was 14.67 plus-or-minus 8.46 degrees and varied markedly by region, reaching 28.76 plus-or-minus 8.84 degrees anteriorly and falling to 8.52 plus-or-minus 3.85 degrees laterally.
Force error was mostly within plus-or-minus 1 N and had reported mean 0.07 plus-or-minus 0.49 N under simulated breathing.

Manual mean CNR values for the three volunteers were 3.01 plus-or-minus 1.01, 3.00 plus-or-minus 1.31, and 3.17 plus-or-minus 1.17; robotic values were 2.78 plus-or-minus 0.90, 2.81 plus-or-minus 0.97, and 3.06 plus-or-minus 1.07, with reported t-test p values 0.21, 0.28, and 0.53.

Because CNR was not used by the surface-normal estimator, it is an example of an independent downstream endpoint; however, manual ROI definition and repeated images nested within targets require leakage-resistant held-out evaluation and clustering-aware analysis.

evidence.locator: Reader assessment of the authors' equivalence interpretation
evidence.finding: Failure to reject a difference in conventional t-tests does not by itself demonstrate equivalence or noninferiority without a predeclared margin and suitable repeated-measures analysis.

boundary_conditions: Four VL53L0X time-of-flight sensors are mounted in a ring and sense surface outside the probe rather than the finite probe-tissue contact patch.
Sensors cannot observe surface within the approximately 35 mm probe-case radius.
Automated motion covers two tilt axes and normal translation; tangential translation and axial rotation remain operator controlled.
Angular commands are empirically tuned PD outputs capped at 0.1 rad/s and updated at up to 30 Hz.
Normal force is estimated from robot joint torque rather than an independent contact-area or distributed-pressure sensor.
Normal-tracking ground truth is provided by motion capture in controlled experiments.
Evaluation uses flat surfaces, an upper-torso mannequin, a breathing phantom, and three volunteers, not human patients or a clinical environment.
The volunteer image study uses eight targets and ten images per target for robotic and freehand scans, creating potential within-target and within-volunteer dependence.
Pleural-line CNR uses a manually defined fixed 10-by-10-pixel ROI and is not part of the online estimator or controller.
No held-out material/geometry shift, nested representation ablation, decision-equivalence margin, or safety-certification protocol is reported.
assumptions: Opposite time-of-flight distance differences provide an adequate empirical error signal for local surface-normal alignment within the sensor geometry.
Lookup-table compensation learned over 50-200 mm remains applicable during the reported tracking experiments.
Moving-average filtering and empirical PD gains provide sufficient real-time behavior for the evaluated motion regimes.
Joint-torque-derived normal force is adequate for the separate landing and force-tracking controller.
Motion-capture normal serves as the relevant geometric ground truth.
The manually selected CNR ROI adequately represents pleural-line visibility for the reported image comparison.

Any use of A-SEE as evidence for SoftScan contact-state design is limited to external geometry sensing and endpoint separation; it does not assume equivalence between nearby surface geometry and finite contact-patch state.

reported: Ambient light can affect the laser range sensors.
The sensors cannot observe the surface within the probe-case radius of approximately 35 mm, contributing to poor accuracy on complex anterior topography.
The current sensor layout may miss limbs or other geometries outside its effective field of view.
Mannequin normal error was markedly worse anteriorly than laterally.
The experiments did not include human patients or a clinical environment and were limited to upper-body simulation and three volunteers.
Controller gains were selected empirically, and miniaturization, sensor-angle changes, human studies, and image-informed orientation were left for future work.
inferred: The system does not establish finite contact-area, pressure-distribution, deformation, tangential-force/moment, or slip-capacity observability because none of those quantities is independently measured.
The reported nonsignificant CNR differences do not establish image-quality equivalence or noninferiority without a predeclared margin and an analysis appropriate for clustered repeated measurements.
Manual ROI selection and target structure could introduce leakage or optimistic assessment unless ROI rules and held-out units are fixed independently of model or controller development.

The work cannot establish the minimally sufficient contact representation or the incremental decision value of contact-patch variables because it contains no nested representation ablation or comparison against force-only and model-agnostic baselines.
The empirical orientation and force controllers do not validate impedance selection under held-out continuous material and geometry shifts.
The study does not provide a safety certificate or evidence for tangential wrench margins, viscoelastic history state, or deployment robustness.

conflicts_with: Conflicts with treating nearby surface-normal measurements as direct observations of finite probe-tissue contact area, pressure, or deformation.
Conflicts with claiming that a nonsignificant difference test alone proves robotic and manual image-quality equivalence.
Conflicts with presenting A-SEE as evidence that external geometry plus normal force is a minimally sufficient contact representation for impedance selection.
Conflicts with treating the study as validation under held-out soft-contact shifts or as evidence of tangential safety margins or clinical deployment safety.
